Ordination biplots

Source: vignettes/ordination.Rmd
ordination.Rmd

An ordination places observations on a small set of axes computed from their measured variables. A biplot draws the observations and variable directions in the same view. stat_biplot_3d() composes site points, solid-headed quiver arrows and optional group regions.

fit <- prcomp(iris[1:4], scale. = TRUE)
groups <- setNames(iris$Species, rownames(iris))
ggplot() + stat_biplot_3d(fit, groups = groups, region = "ellipsoid",
                        loading_scale = 2, label_size = 5) + coord_3d()

For prcomp, sites use fit$x and arrows use fit$rotation. loading_scale explicitly multiplies the arrow vectors for display. The chosen multiplier therefore belongs in a figure’s methods or caption. choices selects the three axes.

Site identifiers are the score matrix’s row names, or sequential character identifiers when row names are absent. Group membership is joined by these identifiers. A named vector or a table with id and group columns can supply membership in any order.

membership <- data.frame(id = names(groups), group = unname(groups))
membership <- membership[rev(seq_len(nrow(membership))), ]
ggplot() + stat_biplot_3d(fit, groups = membership, region = "hull",
                        loading_scale = 2, label_size = 5) + coord_3d()

Vegan scores

vegan supplies ecological ordination methods and a scores() generic that applies their scaling conventions. stat_biplot_3d() calls that generic for vegan fits. Pass method-specific arguments in scores_args, or supply a list containing sites and species score matrices directly.

model <- vegan::rda(iris[1:4], scale = TRUE)
ggplot() + stat_biplot_3d(model, groups = groups,
                        scores_args = list(scaling = 2), label_size = 5) + coord_3d(clip = "off")

The species arrows of this fit reach the edge of the box. clip = "off" lets their labels extend past the drawing area of the panel instead of being cut at its edge.

The group ellipsoids use stat_ellipsoid_3d(type = "norm"). Their level describes the spread of observations under that covariance model. Individual point, quiver, text, hull and ellipsoid layers can also be composed directly when a figure needs separate mappings. vegan3d documents the corresponding ordination and group-region conventions.
